answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, like a garden that only admits members who plant a real deposit. The stake is tied to one verified credential, so spawning thousands of fake identities means locking capital for each one. No ivory-tower audit is needed: peers watch on-chain behavior, and cheaters lose their stake and reputation. Marble-hard economics make fakery expensive while honest agents earn their deposit back, so attack cost scales with the number of fake identities.
